_README: Hand-edited. This is the ONLY file an update to docs/lockout.html ever
requires -- scripts/build_lockout_page.py reads it and regenerates the
page; the daily workflow and a dedicated push-triggered workflow both
run that script, so editing this file and pushing to main is the whole
update. Never hand-edit docs/lockout.html itself.
FIELDS
cba_expires               -- ISO date the current agreement expires.
Not a literal anywhere else on the site;
this file is the one place it is typed.
lockout_start              -- ISO date the lockout began, or null if
no lockout has started yet. Set this the
day it happens and the page switches from
a countdown to a day count automatically.
lockout_end               -- ISO date the lockout ended, or null while
it is ongoing / has not happened.
regular_season_delayed_from -- ISO date the regular season was
originally scheduled to start, or null.
Set this only once games are actually
being missed -- it drives the
'service-time days at stake' figure.
updated                   -- ISO date this file was last hand-edited.
The page shows whichever is newer of this
and the newest entry below.
entries                   -- the update log. Each item needs date
(ISO), headline, summary (plain words, 1-3
sentences, no speculation presented as
fact), source_name and source_url (must be
https). Any order -- the page sorts newest
first on its own.
Never invent a source, a quote, or a date. If nothing new and verified
has happened, don't add an entry.

entries.headline: Reporting: talks remain deadlocked over a salary cap as the Dec. 1 deadline nears
entries.summary: Yahoo Sports reported that with the current agreement expiring Dec. 1, 2026, a lockout is widely expected the next day. The owners' push for a salary cap is described as the central sticking point, with the players' union opposed and instead seeking a higher minimum salary and stronger service-time protections.

entries.headline: Reporting: owners' salary-cap proposal pairs a payroll floor with a 50-50 revenue split
entries.summary: The Boston Globe reported that owners have proposed a salary cap near $245 million together with a roughly $171 million payroll floor and a 50-50 split of revenue, which the players' union has rejected. The two sides are described as deadlocked with the CBA's Dec. 1 expiration approaching.
